payload.rebuttal: argued: The mutated line, contract.py:17 (`_DIGITS = re.compile(r"\d+")`), is pre-existing code my diff never touches; my only change to that file adds the `detail` field near line 59. The probed sentence ('the two details have no digits, so normalize_message cannot make them equal') is the witness's own design rationale, not a separate behavioral claim. The mutant cannot falsify this criterion's real claim, that identity never reads detail, because every pair of identities the test requires to match uses byte-identical message text on both sides ('assert false'/'assert false', 'm'/'m'), and the one pair required to differ (the survivor vs. the baseline failure) differs by file and code ('b.py'/'Y' vs 'a.py'/'X'), not by message content. Any normalization normalize_message applies to message, digit-collapsing or the mutant's whole-word collapsing, is applied identically to equal strings and cannot bridge a file/code difference, so the mutant is orthogonal to this criterion by construction. No detail text in the test is ever read by identity, which is exactly the behavior under test. The mutant is already caught elsewhere in the suite, by test_identity_separates_two_failures_of_the_same_code_in_one_file and test_normalize_message_collapses_whitespace, tests that predate this task and exist to guard _DIGITS for messages that do rely on digit-collapsing. Criterion 2 was never meant to re-guard that regex, and no change to this witness could close the finding, since it isn't a real gap: no edit to _DIGITS can make 'identity never reads detail' false.
